\begin{ealglossed}
\section*{Section 1: \ealgloss{Addition}{جمع} and \ealgloss{Subtraction}{تفریق}}
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Remember:} Line up the \ealgloss{decimal points}{اعشاریہ نقطہ} carefully. When working with \ealgloss{negatives}{منفی}, think about the \ealgloss{sign}{علامت}!
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $45 + 376 =$
    \vspace{2em}
    \item $328.5 + 19.47 =$
    \vspace{2em}
    \item $7.63 + (-2.8) =$
    \vspace{2em}
    \item $-12 + 7 =$
    \vspace{2em}
    \item $56.3 - 18.72 =$
    \vspace{2em}
    \item $-4 - (-9) =$
\end{enumerate}

\begin{ealglossed}
\section*{Section 2: \ealgloss{Multiplication}{ضرب دینا}}
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Remember:} 
\begin{itemize}
    \item Count the \ealgloss{signs}{علامت}: an \ealgloss{even}{جفت} number of \ealgloss{negatives}{منفی} gives a \ealgloss{positive}{مثبت} answer, an \ealgloss{odd}{طاق} number gives a \ealgloss{negative}{منفی} answer.
    \item We need to be careful when multiplying \ealgloss{decimals}{اعشاریہ}, and keep track of the \ealgloss{decimal point}{اعشاریہ نقطہ}, three methods are described below.
\end{itemize}
\end{ealglossed}


\begin{ealglossed}
For the example \ealgloss{multiplication}{ضرب دینا}: $3.4 \times 1.2$, the three options are:
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
\subsection*{1. \ealgloss{Factoring}{عامل} Up to \ealgloss{Whole Numbers}{مکمل عدد}}
\end{ealglossed}


\begin{ealglossed}
We can make both numbers whole by multiplying by \ealgloss{powers}{قوت} of 10. These are $10$, $100$, $1\,000$, $10\,000$, \dots \quad etc.
\end{ealglossed}

Multiply \(3.4\) by \(10\) to make it \(34\).  
Multiply \(1.2\) by \(10\) to make it \(12\).

Now we have:
\[
34 \times 12 = 408
\]

But we multiplied the numbers by \(10 \times 10 = 100\),  
so we divide the answer by \(100\):

\[
\frac{408}{100} = 4.08
\]

---

\begin{ealglossed}
\subsection*{2. Counting \ealgloss{Decimal Places}{اعشاریہ مقام}}
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Multiply the numbers as if there are no \ealgloss{decimal points}{اعشاریہ نقطہ}.  
    \item Count how many \ealgloss{decimal places}{اعشاریہ مقام} there are in total in the question.  
    \item Put that many \ealgloss{decimal places}{اعشاریہ مقام} back into your answer.
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}

\textbf{Example:} \(3.4 \times 1.2\)

\begin{ealglossed}
Ignore the \ealgloss{decimals}{اعشاریہ}: \(34 \times 12 = 408\)
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
There is \textbf{1} \ealgloss{decimal place}{اعشاریہ مقام} in 3.4 and \textbf{1} in 1.2, so \textbf{2 in total.}
\end{ealglossed}

\vspace{1em}

So the answer is \(4.08\) 

---

\begin{ealglossed}
\subsection*{3. Lattice Method with \ealgloss{Decimal}{اعشاریہ} Alignment}
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
You can use the lattice method to track the \ealgloss{decimal points}{اعشاریہ نقطہ} too.
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1.2, every node/.style={font=\small}]

% Grid (2x2 for digits 3,4 × 1,2)
\draw (0,0) rectangle (2,2);
\draw (1,0) -- (1,2);
\draw (0,1) -- (2,1);


\draw (0,0) -- (2,2);
\draw (1,0) -- (2,1);
\draw (0,1) -- (1,2);


% Top numbers (3 and 4)
\node at (0.5,2.2) {3};
\node at (1.5,2.2) {4};

% Side numbers (1 and 2)
\node at (2.2,1.5) {1};
\node at (2.2,0.5) {2};

% Products in cells (tens and ones separated)
% 3×1 = 3, 4×1 = 4, 3×2=6, 4×2=8
\node at (0.3,1.7) {0};
\node at (0.7,1.3) {3};

\node at (1.3,1.7) {0};
\node at (1.7,1.3) {4};

\node at (0.3,0.7) {0};
\node at (0.7,0.3) {6};

\node at (1.3,0.7) {0};
\node at (1.7,0.3) {8};

% Diagonal sums
\node at (1.5,-0.3) {8};
\node at (0.5,-0.3) {0};
\node at (-0.4,0.5) {4};
\node at (-0.4,1.5) {0};

% Decimal point placement
\node at (2.3,1) {\Huge$\cdot$};
\node at (1, 2.15) {\Huge$\cdot$};

% decimal point movement to result

\draw[red, dash pattern=on 2pt off 1pt, ->] (1.02,2.0) -- (1.02,1);
\draw[red, dash pattern=on 2pt off 1pt, ->] (2,1.02) -- (1,1.02);
\draw[red, dash pattern=on 2pt off 1pt, ->] (1.02,1.04) -- (0,0.03);

\node at (-0.1,-0.1) {\Huge$\cdot$};

\end{tikzpicture}

\end{center}


\begin{ealglossed}
Find where the \ealgloss{decimal points}{اعشاریہ نقطہ} in each number meet, then follow the diagonal down to the left, that will be where the \ealgloss{decimal point}{اعشاریہ نقطہ} is in the answer.
\end{ealglossed}

\vspace{1em}

In the example above we get \(4.08\), the same as before!

\begin{ealglossed}
\section*{Section 3: \ealgloss{Division}{تقسیم}}
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Remember:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item Use the bus stop method unless you can do it in your head.
    \item If the \ealgloss{divisor}{تقسیم کنندہ} is a \ealgloss{decimal}{اعشاریہ}, you need to make it a \ealgloss{whole number}{مکمل عدد} (remember to apply the \ealgloss{factor}{عامل} to both numbers!): \newline $ 66 \div 0.33 = 6600 \div 33 = 200 $
    \item Chunk larger \ealgloss{divisors}{تقسیم کنندہ} into smaller \ealgloss{factors}{عامل} if helpful. \newline $176 \div 16 = ( 176 \div 4) \div 4 = 44 \div 4 = 11$
\end{itemize}
\end{ealglossed}

\section*{Extension Word Problems}

\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The temperature was $-3^\circ$C and dropped by $5^\circ$C overnight. What is the new temperature?
    \vspace{2em}
    \item A scuba diver descends $2.5$ m per minute for 4 minutes, then ascends $3$ m. What is the diver’s final depth?
    \vspace{2em}
    \item A submarine starts at sea level and travels vertically $-4.2$ km, then another $-3.8$ km. How far is it from the surface now? What is the submarine's \ealgloss{altitude}{ارتفاع}?
    \vspace{2em}
    \item Some numbers produce \ealgloss{recurring decimals}{تکراری اعشاریہ} when used as \ealgloss{divisors}{تقسیم کنندہ}. Find the \ealgloss{decimal}{اعشاریہ} result of 1 divided by each of the first 7 \ealgloss{prime numbers}{مفرد عدد}. Some results \ealgloss{terminate}{ختم ہونا} while others recur. Can you explain why?
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}
